Cortex

Everything Cortex can do, on one page

Cortex is the Value Consulting team's assistant. It reads client material, scores capability, builds ROI models, writes decks and runs whole assessments. Find what you need below, copy the example, change the words to fit your deal.

Run an Ignite workshop

Ignite Inspire is workshop-driven, so it doesn't touch the assessment pipeline. Prep writes a checkpoint and stops, on purpose — fix the hypotheses before a deck gets built on top of them.

Workshop synthesis“synthesise the workshops”ignite-workshop-synthesizerReads all four workshop outputs, works out which hypotheses held, and ranks the use-case candidates"All four workshops are done — what are our P1 use cases for Ignite Day?"

Finish, share, bank the learning

The last mile. One of these makes the work better; the rest make the next engagement start further ahead.

NameType thisWhat it doesExample
Tear it apart/crittyComingTurns the critical dial to maximum and attacks the work — assumptions, thin evidence, unearned conclusions. It's meant to sting/critty — run it the day before anything important goes out
Publish/publishCommits, pushes and opens a pull request. You never touch git/publish — or just say "publish my changes"
Tidy the queue/reconcileChecks every open pull request for conflicts, merges the clean ones, resolves the rest/reconcile — when reviews are piling up
Bank the learning/extract-learningsPulls the reusable knowledge out of a finished engagement and files it, anonymised/extract-learnings — point it at the closed engagement
Log a fix/log-modificationRecords that you had to fix an output by hand, and why. Thirty seconds that decides what gets improved next/log-modification — "Rewrote the ROI summary again; it buries the headline number."
Knowledge harvestAutomaticFiles anonymised learnings automatically after every pipeline run. Don't call this by handNothing to type — it happens at the end of a run
Pipelines

Run the whole thing

A pipeline is several agents run in order, with you approving at the checkpoints. Reach for one when you want the whole deliverable. If you only want the ROI model or the capability scoring, run that on its own from the table above.

NameType thisWhat it doesExample
Ignite Assess
/run-pipelineThe full evidence-driven assessment: discovery, five analyses in parallel, roadmap, assembly, dashboard, Excel. Hours, not minutes, and real API cost/run-pipeline — point it at an engagement folder with transcripts in inputs/
Ignite Inspire“we're running an Ignite with…”workshop-preparationFour workshops — strategy, member, employee, architecture — each prepared, run, then synthesised into the Ignite Day deck. Not the assessment pipeline; it's driven by the room, not by transcripts"We're running an Ignite with Pacific Credit Union. Start with the strategy workshop."
Hybrid“describe the engagement and let it route”value-consulting-orchestratorAssess and Inspire together, with the workshop priorities feeding the ROI model. The orchestrator works out which you're describing and routes you, so you don't have to pick"We've got transcripts and we're running workshops in March — what should we do first?"
ROI run
/build-roiLevers, then model, then workbook — the money case on its own, without the assessment around it. The most-used pipeline in the team/profile-bank first so the baseline is real, then /build-roi, then /generate-roi-excel
House rules

Six things worth knowing before you start

Client files go in the engagement's inputs/ folder. Never paste a transcript into the chat. That folder is where the scrubber sits — names, account numbers and anything else identifying get stripped before the model sees them. Pasted text goes through exactly as you typed it.

It stops and asks you things. Those stops are the point. Cortex pauses at checkpoints so you can correct it before it builds three more things on top of a wrong assumption. Clicking through quickly to save ten minutes is what costs you an afternoon.

What comes out is a first draft by a very fast analyst, not a finished deliverable. You're still the consultant. Read it before it goes anywhere near a client — especially the assumptions register, which is where it tells you what it had to guess.

Every number should trace back to something. An evidence ID, a sourced benchmark, or a documented assumption. If you find a figure that traces to none of those, that's a bug worth reporting, not something to quietly correct.

Fixed something by hand? Spend thirty seconds on /log-modification. Nobody can see you editing an output. If you fix the same weakness on every engagement and never say so, it stays broken for everyone, forever. It is the cheapest thing anyone on the team can contribute.

You can't break anything. You're always working on your own copy, you never touch git yourself, and nothing reaches the shared repository until /publish opens it for review. Experiment freely.

Start here

New here? This is the whole setup

About half an hour, most of it waiting for a download. You need a laptop, a Backbase GitHub account and a Claude account. You do not need to know how to code, and you never need to use git directly.

1

Get a GitHub account, and access to the repo

Sign up at github.com with your Backbase email if you don't already have an account, then ask Mariam, Mayur or Shobhit to add you to the value-consulting-agents repository. Nothing below works until you can see it.

2

Install Claude Code

Claude Code is the tool that runs Cortex — a chat window that can read and write files on your machine. Get it from claude.ai/code and sign in with your Backbase account. The desktop app is the easiest start; the terminal version is the same thing.

3

Copy the repo onto your laptop

Open Claude Code and ask it: “Clone the Backbase value-consulting-agents repo into my projects folder.” It will walk you through signing in to GitHub the first time. Then open that folder as your working directory.

git clone https://github.com/mayur294-lgtm/value-consulting-agents.git
4

Run the one-time setup

This installs the PII scrubber that keeps client names out of anything Cortex sends outside. It downloads about 380 MB, so give it a few minutes. Until it's done, client documents in inputs/ won't open — that's deliberate.

bash scripts/setup_pii.sh
Full PII setup guide →
5

Start an engagement

One command creates the folder structure, the journal and the intake template. Put client material in the inputs/ folder it makes. You'll never need to remember the folder name — the second command finds it from the client name.

./scripts/init_engagement.sh navy_federal 2026-02_retail_assessment assessment
./scripts/find_engagement.sh navy_federal
6

Do the work

Type a slash command from the table above, or just describe what you want in plain English. Cortex asks before it does anything expensive, and stops at checkpoints so you can steer. When you're finished, /publish saves everything and opens a pull request for review.

Stuck, or something behaved oddly? Say so in the Cortex channel. A confusing output is a bug in the system, not a mistake you made — reporting it is how the next version stops doing it.
